front: Who is my neighbor?
back: Anyone who needs our love and help.

front: A _____ is anyone who needs our love and help.
What question did Jesus answer with the story of the Good Samaritan?
Where in the Bible is the story of the Good Samaritan?
What happened to the traveler in the story?
back: Robbers hurt him and left him on the road.

front: What did the first people who saw the hurt traveler do?
Who stopped to help the hurt traveler?
Why was it surprising that the Samaritan helped?
back: His people and the traveler's people did not get along, but he helped anyway.

front: How did the Samaritan care for the man?
back: He bandaged his wounds and paid for a safe place (an inn) where he could heal.

front: Is my neighbor only the person who lives next door?
back: No. Jesus teaches that a neighbor is anyone who needs our help.

front: Can we be good neighbors to people we don't know yet?
back: Yes. We can help anyone who needs it, even a stranger.

How can you be a good neighbor to a new student?

How can your family help neighbors who need food?
back: Donate food to a food pantry.

front: Which commandment teaches us to respect human life?
What does the Fifth Commandment say?
back: You shall not kill. It teaches us to respect and protect every human life.

front: After doing a good neighbor deed, what can we do?
back: Thank God for the chance to be a good neighbor.
